tb21_profile.skill: Export trained PyTorch weights to a plain serialized format, then hand-implement the forward pass (conv/linear/ReLU/argmax) plus image preprocessing in C and compile it to a working argv-driven binary
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch / MNIST CNN numerics crossed with C systems programming, gcc compilation and PNG pixel decoding
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec, multi-artifact build: produce weights.json + compiled cli_tool binary + prediction.txt whose numbers must match a reference model

notes: final_top10 is entirely TMax-15K and that is the honest answer: only TMax has tasks that hand-implement a NN forward pass from serialized weights in a compiled language, which is the whole TB2.1 task. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the weakest pool: its ~100 MNIST hits are all the same sds-mnist repo-setup chore (clone, venv, pip install sds+numpy, run example) and share only the word MNIST plus a predicted digit in result.txt -- pure lexical false positive, scored 2. Its defensible entries are instead the write-C-and-compile-a-binary tasks. TerminalWorld is thin too: no task there implements model numerics by hand. SWE-Smith reduces almost entirely to fvcore (the one PyTorch-numerics repo in the pool); the many CLI-argparse bug reports the retrievers surfaced (charset_normalizer, wordcloud, pdfminer, click) match only on the word 'CLI' and were rejected. SWE-Rebench contributes keras/pyg weight-serialization bugs, which are real domain transfer but wrong genre.
